newsitem.title: USA: AIG foreign property net premiums up.
newsitem.headline: AIG foreign property net premiums up.

text.p: American International Group Inc said its international property-casualty business has strong underwriting results in the first quarter and said net premiums written rose eight percent, excluding the impact of foreign exchange.
In Japan, where the economy continues to be weak, AIG said growth exceeds that of the domestic property-casualty industry, producing excellent results.
Excluding Japan, international property-casualty net premiums written grew 10.6 percent.
"The deregulation taking place in Japan will soon permit us to introduce new products and distribution methods which should benefit our business there," AIG chairman Maurice Greenberg said.
Continental European operations, including Central Europe, did very well.

"Central Europe represents a sizable growth area for AIG, both in general insurance and life insurance, and we have the most extensive network in the region of any international insurance organization," he said.
He said the network was bolstered this quarter by the acquisition of an interest in a general insurance company in Bulgaria, which has been renamed AIG Bulgaria.
Operations in the United Kingdom were very good, in spite of a continued competitive marketplace, he said.
